h1: The 6 Best Mini Chainsaws Under $150 for Serious Pruning, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Mini Chainsaw Under $150: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 mini chainsaws under $150 from SEESII, Greenworks and DeWalt, compared on bar length, motor type and battery platform.
summary: The SEESII Flagship 8-Inch is the best mini chainsaw under $150 for value, with a brushless motor and an 8 inch bar. The DeWalt DCCS623B is the pick if you already own 20V DeWalt batteries, the Greenworks 24V 10 inch is the larger compact saw, and the Greenworks 6 inch models are the light pruners.
intro: Moving your budget from $50 to $150 does not buy a bigger mini chainsaw so much as a better-engineered one. The hidden tradeoff is the battery. A cheaper saw that includes a battery has an obvious total cost, while a bare-tool model from a major brand only makes sense if you already own that battery platform. Buy the wrong one and the real price doubles.

This ranking compares six saws that fit the under-$150 mark by bar length, motor type, battery platform and what is in the box. We reviewed the listings and brand specifications rather than invent numbers, and the larger 12 inch chainsaws that appeared in the source results were left out because a 12 inch saw is no longer a mini.

products.name: SEESII Flagship 8-Inch Cordless Mini Chainsaw, Upgraded Brushless Motor
products.verdict: An 8 inch bar and a brushless motor for under $100, the best value in the group.
products.description:
The SEESII Flagship pairs an 8 inch bar with an upgraded brushless motor, and it is priced between $50 and $100. That is a long bar and a modern motor for the money.

It wins because the combination suits real pruning work. A brushless motor spends less energy as heat, so a small battery lasts longer per charge, and the 8 inch bar can pass through a limb in one cut rather than rocking back and forth. The listing says nothing about battery count or auto oiling, so check the box contents before ordering, and keep bar oil on hand.

Buy it for regular yard pruning and firewood trimming. Skip it if you want a saw tied to a major tool brand's battery system.
pros: Price is well under the cap
products.idealFor: Regular pruners who want power without a big outlay.
products.skipIf: You want to share batteries with a larger tool range.

products.name: DeWalt Chainsaw Pruning CRDLS 20V 8IN DCCS623B
products.verdict: DeWalt's own 20V pruning chainsaw with an 8 inch bar, best if you already own the batteries.
products.description:
This is DeWalt's 20V 8 inch cordless pruning chainsaw, listed under model number DCCS623B, in the $100 to $200 price tier. DeWalt commonly uses a B suffix for bare tools, so confirm whether a battery and charger are included before you buy.

It ranks second because it comes from a professional-focused tool maker, which means parts, support and a deep battery ecosystem. If you already hold 20V DeWalt batteries, the saw is simple to run and the batteries pull double duty. The cost is a higher entry price, and for anyone starting from nothing the battery adds to the bill.

Choose it if you own DeWalt 20V tools. Skip it if you want a complete kit at the lowest price.
products.idealFor: Owners of DeWalt 20V batteries and tools.
products.skipIf: You want an all-in-one kit with a battery.

products.name: Greenworks 24V 10" Cordless Compact Chainsaw (Great For Storm Clean-Up, Pruning, and Firewood), 2.0Ah Battery and Charger Included
products.verdict: A 10 inch compact saw that includes a 2.0Ah battery and charger for storm clean-up.
products.description:
The Greenworks 24V is a 10 inch compact saw, aimed at storm clean-up, pruning and firewood, with a 2.0Ah battery and charger included. It sits in the $100 to $200 price tier.

It takes third place because the 10 inch bar is a step up in capacity from the 6 and 8 inch saws, and the box contains everything you need. That makes it the most useful all-rounder for anyone with fallen limbs after a storm. It is the biggest saw here, so it is a compromise between a true mini and a small chainsaw, and the 2.0Ah battery is a modest size for longer jobs.

Pick it if you need extra bar length. Skip it if you want the lightest and cheapest pruning saw.
products.idealFor: Homeowners facing storm damage and firewood.
products.skipIf: You want the lightest possible pruning tool.

products.name: Cordless Mini Chainsaw Compatible with Dewalt 20V MAX Battery, 6 Inch & 8 Inch Small Electric Chainsaw Brushless, Auto Oiler
products.verdict: A brushless, auto-oiling third-party saw for DeWalt 20V MAX batteries, sold as tool only.
products.description:
This third-party saw runs on DeWalt 20V MAX batteries and is sold as a bare tool. It lists both 6 inch and 8 inch bars, a brushless motor and an auto oiler, in the $50 to $100 tier.

It ranks fourth because it undercuts the genuine DeWalt saw while adding an auto oiler. For a DeWalt battery owner that can be a clever saving. The risk is fit and support: a third-party tool on a major battery platform depends on the seller for any warranty problem, and the DeWalt brand does not stand behind it.

Buy it if you own spare batteries and want to save money. Skip it if you want official brand support.
pros: Two bar sizes to choose from
products.idealFor: DeWalt battery owners who want to save.

products.name: Greenworks 24V 6in Mini Chainsaw, 2.0 Ah Battery and Charger
products.verdict: A light 6 inch saw with a 2.0 Ah battery and charger, from a known outdoor brand.
products.description:
This Greenworks 24V saw has a 6 inch bar and comes with a 2.0 Ah battery and charger, in the $50 to $100 tier.

It ranks fifth because it is the smallest saw that still arrives ready to run. A 6 inch bar suits thin branches, shrub work and tidy-up jobs where a lighter tool is easier to control. The compromise is reach: you cannot cut through a thick limb in one pass, and the listing gives no motor type.

Buy it for light pruning from a brand with parts and support. Skip it if you regularly cut limbs thicker than a forearm.
pros: Ready to run out of the box
products.idealFor: Light pruners who want a simple kit.

products.name: Greenworks 24V 6 in Mini Pruning Chainsaw, 2.0 Ah Battery and Charger
products.verdict: A near-identical 6 inch Greenworks pruner listed at a higher price tier.
products.description:
This Greenworks 24V 6 in mini pruning chainsaw ships with a 2.0 Ah battery and charger, in the $100 to $200 tier. On paper it matches the other 6 inch Greenworks kit.

It ranks last because the listing shows no extra feature to justify the higher price tier. If it were cheaper than the model above it would rank higher, because the tool category is the same and the brand support identical. Buy based on the lowest price you can find rather than the listing name.

Choose it only if it is the best current deal. Skip it if the other 6 inch Greenworks is cheaper.
cons: Higher price tier than its twin
products.idealFor: Buyers who find it at a good price.
products.skipIf: A cheaper 6 inch Greenworks is available.

whatMatters.detail: The battery is often half the cost of a cordless tool. A saw on a platform you already own, such as DeWalt 20V or Greenworks 24V, saves real money. Check the voltage on the listing and the words tool only or battery included.

A longer bar cuts thicker wood but adds weight and kickback risk. For overhead or one-handed pruning, 6 inch suits best, while 8 to 10 inch fits storm cleanup. Match bar length to the thickest limb you cut regularly.

Brushless motors use electronic control instead of carbon brushes, which reduces heat and wear and extends runtime. They usually cost a little more. On a listing, look for the word brushless in the title rather than relying on a wattage claim.

A chain without oil overheats and dulls rapidly. Auto oilers feed oil during the cut, cutting the chore of stopping to oil by hand. Not every listing mentions this, so check before you buy and stock bar oil either way.

A major tool brand gives you spare chains, bars and a clear warranty route. Third-party saws on a major platform are cheaper, but you depend on the seller. Consider how likely you are to need a replacement part.

faq.q: Is a 10 inch saw still a mini chainsaw?
faq.a: It is a compact chainsaw. The Greenworks 24V 10 inch is the largest saw here, so it bridges a mini pruner and a small chainsaw. Pick it if you need extra reach.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying one of these?
faq.a: Forgetting the battery. A bare tool needs a compatible pack and charger, which can double the cost. Check whether the listing says tool only before you add it to the cart.

faq.q: Is the DeWalt DCCS623B worth it over the SEESII Flagship?
faq.a: If you already own DeWalt 20V batteries, yes, for the brand support. If you are starting fresh, the SEESII costs less and includes a brushless motor.
Usually a few minutes. Fit the bar and chain, tension it, fill the oil reservoir and charge the battery. Read the manual on chain direction, since a reversed chain will not cut.

faq.q: How do I look after the saw?
faq.a: Clean sawdust from the bar groove, keep the oil tank topped up and check chain tension before each session. Store the battery partly charged and away from heat.
It is not recommended. Overhead work risks kickback and falling debris, and a mini chainsaw is not designed for it. Use a pole saw for high branches.

finalTake: The SEESII Flagship 8-Inch is the best mini chainsaw under $150 for most people, with a brushless motor and an 8 inch bar for under $100. The DeWalt DCCS623B suits those already on the DeWalt 20V platform, and the Greenworks 24V 10 inch is the larger option for storm cleanup. Count the battery in your budget before you buy.
